newsitem.title: UK: UK to loosen curbs on mobile phone airtime sales.
newsitem.headline: UK to loosen curbs on mobile phone airtime sales.

text.p: Britain's telecommunications industry watchdog OFTEL said on Wednesday it was cutting some restrictions on how mobile phone operators sell airtime.

OFTEL said in a statement the changes would be implemented for Orange Plc and One2One in around six months. The larger operators, Vodafone Group Plc and Cellnet would be freed later although a review was unlikely before 1998.
UK to loosen curbs on mobile phone airtime sales
OFTEL's director general of telecommunications Don Cruickshank said Britain now had seven million mobile phones and more connections were expected.

"The market has become increasingly competitive. Yet all four operators are still subject to special regulation, in some cases more onerous than that applied to British Telecommunications Plc," Cruickshank said.
He said the operators had only limited freedom to decide how best to distribute their services because of rules set up before they had launched their networks.

Under the changes, Orange and One2One would no longer have to provide airtime wholesale to service providers for resale -- a requirement that OFTEL called an unnecessary restriction on the commercial freedom of operators without market power.
